title: Panch Kedar Yatra: The Five Shiva Temples, Story, Treks & Dates
seo_title: Panch Kedar Yatra: 5 Temples, Story, Treks & Best Time
seo_desc: Panch Kedar guide: Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar and Kalpeshwar — the Pandava legend, treks, 2026 closing dates, route and a sample plan.
label: Panch Kedar
blurb: Five Shiva shrines of the Garhwal Himalaya
sub: Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar and Kalpeshwar — the five Shiva temples of Garhwal joined by one Pandava legend. Which is which, how hard each walk is, the 2026 closing dates, where the deities sit in winter and a sample plan to see all five.
q: What is the Panch Kedar and which five temples are in it?
answer: The Panch Kedar are five Shiva temples in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand: Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar and Kalpeshwar. By tradition, parts of Shiva's bull form appeared at each after he hid from the Pandavas. Four close for winter; Kalpeshwar stays open all year. Seeing all five takes about 12–16 days from Rishikesh, with several mountain treks.

intro: Kedarnath is the best known of the five and a Jyotirlinga — read our full Kedarnath Yatra guide. The other four sit in quieter valleys: Tungnath above the meadows of Chopta, Madhyamaheshwar at the end of a long walk from Ransi, Rudranath in high alpine grassland above Gopeshwar, and Kalpeshwar in the green Urgam valley. Three are in Rudraprayag district (Kedarnath, Tungnath, Madhyamaheshwar) and two in Chamoli (Rudranath, Kalpeshwar).

The Panch Kedar are a different circuit from the Panch Badri and the Panch Prayag, though many pilgrims combine them with Badrinath or the full Char Dham Yatra. Note that the Omkareshwar temple at Ukhimath, where Kedarnath is worshipped in winter, is not the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh. See all our guides on the pilgrimage tours page.

story.h2: The Panch Kedar legend: Shiva and the Pandavas
story.lead: This is the tradition of the Mahabharata cycle and the Kedar Khand of the Skanda Purana, retold in our own words — a belief held with love, not history.
beats: After the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas set out to ask Shiva's forgiveness for the killing of their own kin.
Shiva did not wish to be found so easily. He left Kashi and hid in the Garhwal hills as a bull — the place near which he hid is called Guptkashi, the hidden Kashi.
The brothers recognised him in a herd. Bhima stood astride two hills so the cattle had to pass below, and as the bull sank into the earth he caught hold of its back.

The hump stayed at Kedarnath. It is believed the arms appeared at Tungnath, the face at Rudranath, the navel at Madhyamaheshwar and the matted hair at Kalpeshwar — and the Pandavas built a shrine at each.
more: One tradition adds that the head appeared at Pashupatinath in Nepal. Lists of the parts differ a little from one telling to another — Madhyamaheshwar is sometimes called the middle or belly — so read them as tradition, not a fixed record.

route.h2: The Panch Kedar route by road and on foot
route.lead: Road distances are approximate and hill roads are slow. Traditionally the order is Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar, Kalpeshwar; many pilgrims follow the road order below instead.
stops: Five to six hours of hill driving up the Alaknanda and Mandakini valleys. Ukhimath is the base and the winter seat of Kedarnath and Madhyamaheshwar.
Shuttle to Gaurikund, then about 16 km on foot to Kedarnath (pony, palki or IRCTC helicopter).
Drive from Ukhimath to the road head at Ransi and walk about 16 km via Gaundar to the temple.
About 3.5 km on a short but steep path to Tungnath; Chandrashila peak is about 1.5 km further.
From Sagar near Gopeshwar, about 18–20 km up through forest and high meadows to Rudranath — the hardest walk.
Turn into the Urgam valley; Kalpeshwar is a short walk from the road head.
route.note: Rudranath and Madhyamaheshwar are multi-day treks for fit walkers with a guide. Avoid the monsoon (July–August), when landslides often block these roads.

reach.h2: How to reach the Panch Kedar
cards: Jolly Grant airport, Dehradun, is the nearest. Rishikesh is a short drive away, and the hill journey to Ukhimath starts there.
Rishikesh and Haridwar stations (Haridwar–Rishikesh about 24 km). Most trips start from either town early in the morning.
Rishikesh to Ukhimath is about 216 km. Chopta, Sonprayag, Ransi and Gopeshwar are all reached from there — see the route above. For a car, our Rishikesh taxi page has options.
A helicopter runs only for Kedarnath — book it only on heliyatra.irctc.co.in. Ponies and porters work on most of the trails; confirm rates at the counters.

items: Kedarnath needs the Uttarakhand Char Dham registration on registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in. No separate registration is reported for the other four — check the Uttarakhand portal and temple committee notices before you go. Ignore anyone selling "confirmed" passes or helicopter tickets.
Kedarnath (with pony or helicopter), Tungnath (short but steep) and Kalpeshwar (a short walk) are realistic for most families. Rudranath and Madhyamaheshwar are for fit trekkers.
Four of the five temples are above about 3,400 m. Walk slowly, drink water and see a doctor first if you have heart, breathing or blood-pressure problems.
May–June and September–October. In winter you can still pray at the winter seats — Ukhimath, Makkumath, Gopeshwar — and at Kalpeshwar, all by road.
Photo ID and your Kedarnath registration; warm layers, a rain shell, grippy shoes and a stick; a torch, personal medicines and some cash, as networks are patchy.

itinerary.h2: A sample 13-day Panch Kedar plan from Rishikesh
days: Rishikesh → Ukhimath
About 216 km. Evening darshan at the Omkareshwar temple.
Ukhimath → Gaurikund → Kedarnath
Drive to Sonprayag, shuttle to Gaurikund and walk about 16 km to Kedarnath.
Kedarnath → Sonprayag
Morning darshan, walk down and drive back towards Ukhimath.
Ransi → Gaundar
Drive to Ransi and walk to the halt at Gaundar.
Madhyamaheshwar
Walk up to the temple for darshan and stay the night.
Madhyamaheshwar → Ukhimath
Walk back to Ransi and drive to Ukhimath or Chopta.
Tungnath and Chandrashila
Early walk from Chopta to Tungnath, on to Chandrashila for the sunrise peaks, and back.
Chopta → Gopeshwar
About 44 km. Darshan at the Gopinath temple.
Sagar → Rudranath trail
Start the long walk from Sagar with a guide and halt on the way.
Rudranath
Darshan at Rudranath, where Shiva is worshipped as the face.
Rudranath → Gopeshwar
Walk down to Sagar and drive back to Gopeshwar.
Kalpeshwar
Drive about 55 km to Helang, into the Urgam valley, and walk to Kalpeshwar.
Return
Long drive back towards Rishikesh, or keep it as a spare day for weather.

faqs: What are the Panch Kedar temples?
Five Shiva temples in the Garhwal Himalaya: Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar and Kalpeshwar. By tradition, parts of Shiva's bull form appeared at each.
What is the Panch Kedar story?
According to tradition, the Pandavas sought Shiva's pardon after the Kurukshetra war. He hid from them as a bull, sank into the earth when found, and parts of his body appeared at five places.
Which Panch Kedar temple is open all year?
Kalpeshwar, in the Urgam valley of Chamoli district. The other four close for winter.
Which is the highest Panch Kedar temple?
Tungnath, at about 3,680 m — widely regarded as the highest Shiva temple in the world. The walk from Chopta is about 3.5 km.
Which Panch Kedar trek is the hardest?
Rudranath, about 18–20 km from Sagar near Gopeshwar, followed by Madhyamaheshwar, about 16 km from Ransi.
When did the Panch Kedar temples close in 2026?

Rudranath closed in mid-October, Tungnath on 6 November and Kedarnath on 11 November; Madhyamaheshwar closed on 16 November 2026, and its doli reached the Omkareshwar temple at Ukhimath on 19 November. Kalpeshwar stays open.
How many days does the Panch Kedar Yatra take?
About 12–16 days from Rishikesh for all five, depending on weather, fitness and the order you choose.
Where are the Panch Kedar deities worshipped in winter?
Kedarnath and Madhyamaheshwar at the Omkareshwar temple, Ukhimath; Tungnath at Makkumath; Rudranath at the Gopinath temple, Gopeshwar.
